# ============================================================
# HMDA + Census Data Cleaning (R)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# This script:
#   1. Pulls tract-level rent-burden data from Census ACS via tidycensus
#   2. Reads and cleans the HMDA CSV you downloaded manually from
#      https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/data-browser/
#   3. Joins them on census tract
#   4. Exports one clean CSV for the Python modeling step
#
# Before running, install packages (one time only):
#   install.packages(c("tidycensus", "tidyverse", "janitor"))
#
# You also need a free Census API key (same one you already got):
#   https://api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html
# ============================================================

library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)

# ---------------- CONFIG - edit these ----------------
census_api_key("e2fa3c793c7dd3f60624c5e45710133f62509952", install = FALSE)
STATE <- "IL"                          # two-letter state code
HMDA_FILE <- "actions_taken_1-3_state_IL.csv"  # path to the file you downloaded manually
OUTPUT_FILE <- "hmda_census_cleaned.csv"
# -------------------------------------------------------


# ---- Step 1: Pull tract-level rent burden data ----
# B25070_001 = total renter households
# B25070_010 = renters paying 50%+ of income on rent (severely burdened)
# B19013_001 = median household income
census_raw <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = c(
    total_renters = "B25070_001",
    severely_burdened = "B25070_010",
    median_income = "B19013_001"
  ),
  state = STATE,
  year = 2022,          # latest ACS 5-year estimate at time of writing
  output = "wide"
)

census_clean <- census_raw %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  transmute(
    geoid = geoid,
    rent_burden_pct = (severely_burdened_e / total_renters_e) * 100,
    median_household_income = median_income_e
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rent_burden_pct))   # drop tracts with no renter data

cat("Pulled", nrow(census_clean), "census tracts.\n")


# ---- Step 2: Read and clean the HMDA CSV ----
hmda_raw <- read_csv(HMDA_FILE, guess_max = 100000) %>%
  clean_names()   # converts column names to snake_case, e.g. "Census Tract" -> census_tract

# Basic cleaning: drop rows with missing tract, standardize the tract ID
# to an 11-digit zero-padded string so it matches the census GEOID format
hmda_clean <- hmda_raw %>%
  filter(!is.na(census_tract)) %>%
  mutate(
    census_tract = str_pad(as.character(census_tract), width = 11, pad = "0"),
    # Standardize the target variable: 1 = approved, 0 = denied
    approved = if_else(action_taken == 1, 1, 0)
  ) %>%
  # Drop obvious placeholder/invalid codes some HMDA fields use (e.g. 9999)
  filter(income < 9999 | is.na(income))

cat("Cleaned", nrow(hmda_clean), "HMDA records.\n")


# ---- Step 3: Join on census tract ----
final <- hmda_clean %>%
  left_join(census_clean, by = c("census_tract" = "geoid"))

match_rate <- mean(!is.na(final$rent_burden_pct))
cat(sprintf("Joined %.1f%% of HMDA records to a census tract.\n", match_rate * 100))


# ---- Step 4: Export for Python ----
write_csv(final, OUTPUT_FILE)
cat("Saved cleaned + joined dataset to", OUTPUT_FILE, "\n")

colnames(hmda_raw)
